title: Foundation Models framework
lede: Apple's Foundation Models framework is a Swift API for putting language models in apps, now covering its on-device model, Private Cloud Compute and third-party servers such as Claude and Gemini.

points: Any provider can ship a Swift package conforming to the Language Model protocol, keeping tool calling and guided generation.
Multimodal prompts accept images, and Vision tools such as OCR and barcode reading run on-device.
Dynamic Profiles swap model, temperature, reasoning level and tools within one session while sharing the transcript.
Small Business Program members under two million first-time downloads can use the Private Cloud Compute models at no API cost.
An Evaluations framework, an fm CLI in macOS 27 and a Python SDK round it out.

points.text: Readers parse the Private Cloud Compute offer, with one calling it free samples of tokens.
One user finds the on-device model capable for fixing terminal commands on an 8 GB M1; a reply finds its safety limits aggressive.
Coding is a weak spot: one tester says even the Private Cloud Compute model struggled to build a simple platformer.
Others note Claude supports App Attest, letting iOS apps call models without shipping a key.
